podcast.title: Anger at Bono Post-Live Aid (July 13, 1985)
podcast.body: Adam Clayton expressed anger towards Bono after U2's Live Aid set due to Bono's "grandstanding" and inability to stick to the performance plan, which caused them to miss playing one of their songs. "The Edge, Larry and Adam were furious with Bono's grandstanding and his inability to stick with the plan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Inability to Perform in Sydney (1993)
podcast.body: On November 26, 1993, Adam Clayton was scheduled to play the first of two nights at Sydney Football Stadium, a show intended as a rehearsal for a globally broadcast event. However, he was too intoxicated to take the stage, necessitating his bass tech, Edward Morgan, to fill in for him. "But Adam was way too drunk to be on stage."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Personal Struggles on Zoo TV Tour (1993)
podcast.body: During U2's 1993 Zoo TV tour in Australia, bassist Adam Clayton was in distress following a breakup with model Naomi Campbell. His emotional state led to a three-day bender, which he later admitted to having little memory of after an initial two glasses of wine. "This player Adam Clayton was not doing well. He just broken up with model Naomi Campbell over the phone and was not in good shape."

xref.title: Fill-in Performance for U2 (1993)
xref.body: Edward Morgan successfully filled in for Adam Clayton on bass during a U2 concert at the Sydney Football Stadium on November 26, 1993. This performance marked the only time U2 has performed with a substitute member. "Now that first show went off just fine."

xref.title: Bass Tech for Adam Clayton
xref.body: Edward Morgan served as the bass tech for U2's Adam Clayton. In an emergency on November 26, 1993, during the Zoo TV tour in Sydney, Morgan stepped in to play bass for U2 when Clayton was too drunk to perform. "He was up to a Rody Adam's base text to Edward Morgan to fill in."

xref.title: Forming U2 – The Bulletin Board Note
xref.body: At age 15, frustrated with formal lessons, Larry Mullen pinned a note to the bulletin board at Mount Temple High School in Dublin. The note sought out other musicians who had "wasted money" on guitars. This initiative led him to approach Adam Clayton, and later attracted Dave and Dick Evans (The Edge) and Paul Husson (Bono), leading to the band's first rehearsal in Larry's kitchen in the autumn of 1976. "one day when he was 15 Larry pinned a note to the bulldozen board at Mount Temple High School in Dublin The note said money wasted on a drum kit Were there others out there who had wasted money on guitars."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
